senses.gloss:
Kraivya. Pāñcāla, the king of the Krivis, is mentioned in the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa as having performed the aśvamedha, or horse sacrifice, on the parivakrā. Eggeling, however, takes the word as a proper name, ‘Kraivya, the pāñcāla king.’
Foot notes So the St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.; Weber, Indian Literature, 125, n.; Oldenberg, Buddha, 409, n.
xiii. 5, 4, 7.
Sacred Books of the East, 44, 397 (but cf. p. 398, top).
